Our main technical contributions are: (i) a one-shot lower bound on the Bayes error in simple binary hypothesis testing that satisfies a crucial tensorisation property; (ii) a streamlined proof of the formula for the sample complexity of simple binary hypothesis testing without constraints, first established in arXiv:2403.16981; and (iii) a reverse data-processing inequality for Hellinger-$λ$ divergences, generalising the results from arXiv:1812.03031 and arXiv:2206.02765.

papers.title: The empirical discrete copula process
papers.abstract: This paper develops a general inferential framework for discrete copulas on finite supports in any dimension. The copula of a multivariate discrete distribution is defined as Csiszar's I-projection (i.e., the minimum-Kullback-Leibler divergence projection) of its joint probability array onto the polytope of uniform-margins probability arrays of the same size, and its empirical estimator is obtained by applying that same projection to the array of empirical frequencies observed on the sample. Under the assumption of random sampling, strong consistency and $\sqrt{n}$-asymptotic normality of the empirical copula array is established. The theory is illustrated by deriving the large-sample distribution of Yule's concordance coefficient (the natural analogue of Spearman's $ρ$ for bivariate discrete distributions) and by constructing a test for quasi-independence in multivariate contingency tables.

papers.title: SVarM: Linear Support Varifold Machines for Classification and Regression on Geometric Data
papers.abstract: Despite progress in the rapidly developing field of geometric deep learning, performing statistical analysis on geometric data--where each observation is a shape such as a curve, graph, or surface--remains challenging due to the non-Euclidean nature of shape spaces, which are defined as equivalence classes under invariance groups. Building machine learning frameworks that incorporate such invariances, notably to shape parametrization, is often crucial to ensure generalizability of the trained models to new observations. This work proposes \textit{SVarM} to exploit varifold representations of shapes as measures and their duality with test functions $h:\mathbb{R}^n \times S^{n-1} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$. This method provides a general framework akin to linear support vector machines but operating instead over the infinite-dimensional space of varifolds. We develop classification and regression models on shape datasets by introducing a neural network-based representation of the trainable test function $h$. This approach demonstrates strong performance and robustness across various shape graph and surface datasets, achieving results comparable to state-of-the-art methods while significantly reducing the number of trainable parameters.

papers.title: Fine-Tuning Next-Scale Visual Autoregressive Models with Group Relative Policy Optimization
papers.abstract: Fine-tuning pre-trained generative models with Reinforcement Learning (RL) has emerged as an effective approach for aligning outputs more closely with nuanced human preferences. In this paper, we investigate the application of Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) to fine-tune next-scale visual autoregressive (VAR) models. Our empirical results demonstrate that this approach enables alignment to intricate reward signals derived from aesthetic predictors and CLIP embeddings, significantly enhancing image quality and enabling precise control over the generation style. Interestingly, by leveraging CLIP, our method can help VAR models generalize beyond their initial ImageNet distribution: through RL-driven exploration, these models can generate images aligned with prompts referencing image styles that were absent during pre-training. In summary, we show that RL-based fine-tuning is both efficient and effective for VAR models, benefiting particularly from their fast inference speeds, which are advantageous for online sampling, an aspect that poses significant challenges for diffusion-based alternatives.

papers.title: FreshRetailNet-50K: A Stockout-Annotated Censored Demand Dataset for Latent Demand Recovery and Forecasting in Fresh Retail
papers.abstract: Accurate demand estimation is critical for the retail business in guiding the inventory and pricing policies of perishable products. However, it faces fundamental challenges from censored sales data during stockouts, where unobserved demand creates systemic policy biases. Existing datasets lack the temporal resolution and annotations needed to address this censoring effect. To fill this gap, we present FreshRetailNet-50K, the first large-scale benchmark for censored demand estimation. It comprises 50,000 store-product time series of detailed hourly sales data from 898 stores in 18 major cities, encompassing 863 perishable SKUs meticulously annotated for stockout events. The hourly stock status records unique to this dataset, combined with rich contextual covariates, including promotional discounts, precipitation, and temporal features, enable innovative research beyond existing solutions. We demonstrate one such use case of two-stage demand modeling: first, we reconstruct the latent demand during stockouts using precise hourly annotations. We then leverage the recovered demand to train robust demand forecasting models in the second stage. Experimental results show that this approach achieves a 2.73% improvement in prediction accuracy while reducing the systematic demand underestimation from 7.37% to near-zero bias. With unprecedented temporal granularity and comprehensive real-world information, FreshRetailNet-50K opens new research directions in demand imputation, perishable inventory optimization, and causal retail analytics. The unique annotation quality and scale of the dataset address long-standing limitations in retail AI, providing immediate solutions and a platform for future methodological innovation. The data (https://huggingface.co/datasets/Dingdong-Inc/FreshRetailNet-50K) and code (https://github.com/Dingdong-Inc/frn-50k-baseline}) are openly released.

papers.title: A Pöschl--Teller approximation to the wave equation outside a torus
papers.abstract: We construct a short-time parametrix for the exterior Dirichlet wave equation on the complement of a solid torus. The construction involves freezing one coefficient of the conjugated Laplacian. This results in a family of radial Pöschl--Teller equations. We bound the $L^2$ error in terms of the energy of the initial data. We then give several examples of Gaussian wavepackets in toroidal coordinates.

papers.title: Stable Nonlinear Dynamical Approximation with Dynamical Sampling
papers.abstract: We present a nonlinear dynamical approximation method for time-dependent Partial Differential Equations (PDEs). The approach makes use of parametrized decoder functions, and provides a general, and principled way of understanding and analyzing stability and accuracy of nonlinear dynamical approximations. The parameters of these functions are evolved in time by means of projections on finite dimensional subspaces of an ambient Hilbert space related to the PDE evolution. For practical computations of these projections, one usually needs to sample. We propose a dynamical sampling strategy which comes with stability guarantees, while keeping a low numerical complexity. We show the effectiveness of the method on several examples in moderate spatial dimension.

papers.title: Characterization and Decidability of FC-Definable Regular Languages
papers.abstract: FC is a first-order logic that reasons over all factors of a finite word using concatenation, and can define non-regular languages like that of all squares (ww). In this paper, we establish that there are regular languages that are not FC-definable. Moreover, we give a decidable characterization of the FC-definable regular languages in terms of algebra, automata, and regular expressions. The latter of which is natural and concise: Star-free generalized regular expressions extended with the Kleene star of terminal words.

papers.title: Characterisation of Markov property on planar maps
papers.abstract: We revisit, in a self contained way, the Markov property on planar maps and decorated planar maps from three perspectives. First, we characterize the laws on these planar maps that satisfy both the Markov property and rerooting invariance, showing that they are Boltzmann-type maps. Second, we provide a comprehensive characterization of random submaps, that we call stopping maps, satisfying the Markov property, demonstrating that they are not restricted to those obtained through a peeling procedure. Third, we introduce decorated metric planar maps in which edges are replaced by copies of random length intervals $[0,w_e]$, and the decorations are given by continuous functions on the edges. We define a probability measure on them that is the analogue of the Boltzmann map and show that it satisfies the Markov property even for sets that halt exploration mid-edge.

papers.title: Adaptive Entanglement Distillation
papers.abstract: Quantum network applications impose a variety of requirements on entanglement resources in terms of rate, fidelity, latency, and more. The repeaters in the quantum network must combine good methods for entanglement generation, effective entanglement distillation, and smart routing protocols to satisfy these application requirements. In this work, we focus on entanglement distillation in a linear chain of quantum repeaters. While conventional approaches reuse the same distillation scheme over multiple hop lengths after entanglement swaps, we propose a novel adaptive quantum error correction (QEC) scheme that boosts end-to-end metrics. Specifically, depending on the network operating point, we adapt the code used in distillation over successive rounds to monotonically increase the rate while also improving fidelity. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this strategy using three codes, with parameters [[9,1,3]], [[9,2,3]], [[9,3,3]], and a new performance metric, efficiency, that incorporates both overall rate and fidelity. Since the minimum input fidelity for QEC-based distillation is high, we then extend our study to include non-QEC-based purification protocols, specifically DEJMPS since it outperforms others. We compare the performance of end-to-end DEJMPS against adapting from DEJMPS to QEC once DEJMPS improves the initial fidelity to the threshold for QEC. Through a refined efficiency metric, we illuminate the regime where QEC is beneficial. These results provide a detailed outlook for entanglement purification and distillation in first and second generation quantum repeaters.

papers.title: The Locality of Quantum Theory Does Not Require Complex Numbers
papers.abstract: Complex numbers are central to the standard formulation of quantum theory, but whether they are fundamentally necessary remains unsettled. Familiar real formulations reproduce quantum predictions but fail to be representation-local: local physical operations need not correspond to local entities in the mathematical representation. Here we show that representation-local formulations based solely on real numbers nevertheless exist. Our construction is based on the observation that not every structural feature of finite-dimensional density-matrix quantum theory over the complex numbers need be retained in a real formulation. Specifically, we reconsider two features inherited from the complex formalism: the use of the Kronecker product as the system-combination rule and the representation of states and effects by positive semidefinite matrices. Relaxing only one of these assumptions at a time, we first obtain a representation-local real quantum theory with a modified combination rule that closely parallels the conventional complex formulation. We then show that even with the usual Kronecker-product rule a representation-local real formulation exists, provided states and effects are not required to be positive.

papers.title: Monodromy factorizations of lines on del Pezzo surfaces
papers.abstract: We give a list of monodromy factorizations in the pure mapping class group $PMod(T_{d+1})$ of a torus with d+1 marked points that represent lines on a del Pezzo surface Y of degree $d\le4$. These factorizations are lifts of a certain fixed monodromy factorization in $PMod(T_d)$ that represents Y. In the case d=1, discussed in more detail, we give an explicit correspondence between such factorizations and the 240 roots of $E_8=K^\perp$, the orthogonal complement in $H_2(Y)$ of the canonical class.

papers.title: Gravitational Landscapes: black holes with linear equations of state in asymptotically safe gravity
papers.abstract: We study black holes with linear equation of state within the framework of asymptotically safe gravity. This study extends previous work on gravitational collapse in asymptotically safe gravity (that has been done for a dust fluid) by considering into account the pressure of stellar matter. We derive modified field equations containing the running gravitational coupling and the cosmological constant as functions of energy density. The interior space-time of collapsing star is modeled by the Friedmann-Lemaître-Robertson-Walker metric, while the exterior is described by a static spherically symmetric space-time. Different equations of state from ordinary matter to exotic phantom energy are considered to investigate their impact on black hole structure and horizon formation. Our results illustrate that asymptotically safe gravity can introduce non-singular black hole solutions under specific conditions. These results provide new insights into black hole physics and the avoidance of singularities within the asymptotically safe gravity framework.

papers.title: Dynamics and stability of U(1) spin liquids beyond mean-field theory: Triangular-lattice $J_1$-$J_2$ Heisenberg model
papers.abstract: Quantum spin liquids (QSLs) are long-range entangled phases of frustrated magnets exhibiting fractionalised spin excitations. In two dimensions, there is limited analytical understanding of their excitation spectra beyond parton mean-field theories, which fail to capture many features of the finite frequency dynamical response. We use a self-consistent mean-field theory combined with the random phase approximation (RPA) for the $J_1$-$J_2$ Heisenberg model on the triangular lattice to describe the strong spinon-spinon interactions of the U(1) Dirac QSL. We obtain quantitative results for the dynamical spin structure factor and phase diagram compatible with comprehensive numerical efforts. We show the continuum response at the Brillouin zone corners is described by a spinon-exciton hybridised with monopole gauge excitations. We further show that the transition from the QSL to 120-degree coplanar order is in the QED$_3$ O(3)-GN universality class. We extend the method to chiral QSLs and XXZ anisotropy, and discuss its broad range of applicability to other models and for describing inelastic neutron scattering experiments in KYbSe$_2$.

papers.title: Mitigating transients in flux-control signals in a superconducting quantum processor
papers.abstract: Flux-tunable qubits and couplers are common components in superconducting quantum processors. However, dynamically controlling these elements via current pulses poses challenges due to distortions and transients in the propagating signals. In particular, long-time transients can persist, adversely affecting subsequent qubit control operations. We model the flux control line as a first-order RC circuit and introduce a class of pulses designed to mitigate long-time transients. We theoretically demonstrate the robustness of these pulses against parameter mischaracterization and provide experimental evidence of their effectiveness in mitigating transients when applied to a flux-tunable qubit coupler. The proposed pulse design offers a practical solution for mitigating long-time transients, enabling efficient and reliable experiment tune-ups without requiring detailed flux line characterization.

papers.title: Positionality of Dumont--Thomas numeration systems for integers
papers.abstract: Introduced in 2001 by Lecomte and Rigo, abstract numeration systems provide a way of expressing natural numbers with words from a language $L$ accepted by a finite automaton. As it turns out, these numeration systems are not necessarily positional, i.e., we cannot always find a sequence $U=(U_i)_{i\ge 0}$ of integers such that the value of every word in the language $L$ is determined by the position of its letters and the first few values of $U$. Finding the conditions under which an abstract numeration system is positional seems difficult in general. In this paper, we thus consider this question for a particular sub-family of abstract numeration systems called Dumont--Thomas numeration systems. They are derived from substitutions and were introduced in 1989 by Dumont and Thomas. We exhibit conditions on the underlying substitution so that the corresponding Dumont--Thomas numeration is positional. We first work in the most general setting, then particularize our results to some practical cases. Finally, we link our numeration systems to existing literature, notably properties studied by Rényi in 1957, Parry in 1960, Bertrand-Mathis in 1989, and Fabre in 1995.

papers.title: SWAPPER: Dynamic Operand Swapping in Non-commutative Approximate Circuits for Online Error Reduction
papers.abstract: Error-tolerant applications, such as multimedia processing, machine learning, signal processing, and scientific computing can still produce satisfactory results under approximate computation. Approximate computing (AxC) is a well-established paradigm that improves efficiency by judiciously reducing computation quality, and has been widely applied to arithmetic circuits by modifying their logic behavior. However, depending on the approximation, arithmetic properties, such as commutativity, may no longer hold, causing error accumulation and making the output depend on the operand order. In this work, we show that controlling operand order in non-commutative approximate circuits can significantly reduce computational errors. We propose SWAPPER, a lightweight approach that drastically reduces approximation error by dynamically reordering input operands using only a single bit for the decision. To identify the most effective bit for swapping, we propose a framework applicable at different granularities, achieving large error reductions and significant accuracy gains. We evaluate SWAPPER at both component and application levels: at the component level, it reduces the mean absolute error by up to 50%, and at the application level it achieves up to 90% error reduction for AxBench suite and 66.7% top-1 improvement on a Vision Transformer.

papers.title: Adaptive Lipschitz-Free Proximal Gradient Methods for Stochastic Composite Nonconvex Optimization
papers.abstract: We propose {\sf ALFPG}, an Adaptive Lipschitz-Free Proximal Gradient framework for stochastic composite nonconvex minimization. It adapts stepsizes from the optimization trajectory without requiring smoothness constants or line search. For finite-sum problems, {\sf ALFPG-FS} combines coordinate-wise stepsizes, Nesterov extrapolation, and a SPIDER estimator; {\sf ALFPG-D} is its full-batch specialization. Under component-wise smoothness, bounded sublevel sets, and separate lower bounds on $f$ and $h$, {\sf ALFPG-FS} achieves expected $ε$-stationarity with $\mathcal O(N+\sqrt N ε^{-2})$ component-gradient evaluations. For expectation problems, we develop {\sf ALFPG-MVR1} and {\sf ALFPG-MVR2} (MVR: Momentum-based Variance Reduction). Both use one fresh sample per iteration. MVR1 uses one stochastic-gradient evaluation; MVR2 uses at most two evaluations at different points with the same sample. MVR1 requires smoothness of the expected loss; MVR2 additionally requires uniformly smooth sample losses. When the regularizer is convex or Lipschitz continuous on its effective domain and stochastic gradients are almost surely bounded, both methods achieve expected $ε$-stationarity using $\widetilde{\mathcal O}(σ^2ε^{-4}+ε^{-2})$ and $\widetilde{\mathcal O}(σε^{-3}+ε^{-2})$ stochastic-gradient evaluations, respectively. Here, $N$ is the number of component functions, $σ^2$ bounds the gradient noise variance, and $\widetilde{\mathcal O}$ hides polylogarithmic factors. Neither expectation variant requires prior knowledge of $σ$, and both recover $\widetilde{\mathcal O}(ε^{-2})$ complexity in the zero-noise regime. Numerical experiments on sparse phase retrieval, linear eigenvalue problems, and neural network regression show that all four ALFPG variants generally outperform state-of-the-art proximal-gradient baselines.

papers.title: On coarse tree decompositions and coarse balanced separators
papers.abstract: It is known that there is a linear dependence between the treewidth of a graph and its balanced separator number: the smallest integer $k$ such that for every weighing of the vertices, the graph admits a balanced separator of size at most $k$. We investigate whether this connection can be lifted to the setting of coarse graph theory, where both the bags of the considered tree decompositions and the considered separators should be coverable by a bounded number of bounded-radius balls. As the first result, we prove that if an $n$-vertex graph $G$ admits balanced separators coverable by $k$ balls of radius $r$, then $G$ also admits tree decompositions ${\cal T}_1$ and ${\cal T}_2$ such that: - in ${\cal T}_1$, every bag can be covered by $O(k\log n)$ balls of radius $r$; and - in ${\cal T}_2$, every bag can be covered by $O(k^2\log k)$ balls of radius $r(\log k+\log\log n+O(1))$. As the second result, we show that if we additionally assume that $G$ has doubling dimension at most $m$, then the functional equivalence between the existence of small balanced separators and of tree decompositions of small width can be fully lifted to the coarse setting. Precisely, we prove that for a positive integer $r$ and a graph $G$ of doubling dimension at most $m$, the following conditions are equivalent, with constants $k_1,k_2,k_3,k_4,Δ_3,Δ_4$ depending on each other and on $m$: - $G$ admits balanced separators consisting of $k_1$ balls of radius $r$; - $G$ has a tree decomposition with bags coverable by $k_2$ balls of radius $r$; - $G$ has a tree-partition of maximum degree $\leq Δ_3$ with bags coverable by $k_3$ balls of radius $r$; - $G$ is quasi-isometric to a graph of maximum degree $\leq Δ_4$ and tree-partition width $\leq k_4$.

papers.title: Strichartz estimates for the half Klein-Gordon equation on asymptotically flat backgrounds and applications to cubic Dirac equations
papers.abstract: The aim of this paper is to establish the $L^2_t$-endpoint Strichartz estimate for (half) Klein-Gordon equations on a weakly asymptotically flat space-time. As an application we prove small data global well-posedness and scattering for massive cubic Dirac equations in the full subcritical range in this setting. Crucial ingredient is a parametrix contruction following the work of Metcalfe-Tataru and Xue and complements Strichartz estimates obtained by Zheng-Zhang. The proof of the global result for the cubic Dirac equation follows the strategy developed by Machihara-Nakanishi-Ozawa in the Euclidean setting.

papers.title: Generalized De Bruijn Words, Invertible Necklaces, and the Burrows-Wheeler Transform
papers.abstract: We define generalized de Bruijn words as those words having a Burrows--Wheeler transform that is a concatenation of permutations of the alphabet. We show that generalized de Bruijn words are in one-to-one correspondence with Hamiltonian cycles in the generalized de Bruijn graphs, introduced in the early 1980s in the context of network design. We prove that generalized de Bruijn words retain the asymptotically maximal factor complexity of ordinary de Bruijn words over a fixed alphabet. We then use this class to construct an infinite binary family on which the Burrows--Wheeler transform reduces this complexity from asymptotically maximal to the constant $2$. In particular, this shows that the BWT can substantially improve dictionary compressibility. When the size of the alphabet is a prime $p$, we define invertible necklaces as those whose BWT-matrix is nonsingular. We show that invertible necklaces of length $n$ correspond to normal bases of the finite field $\mathbb{F}_{p^n}$, and that they form an abelian group isomorphic to the Reutenauer group $RG_p^n$. Using known results in abstract algebra, we can establish a connection between generalized de Bruijn words and invertible necklaces. In particular, we highlight a correspondence between binary de Bruijn words of order $d+1$, binary necklaces of length $2^{d}$ having an odd number of $1$'s, invertible BWT matrices of size $2^{d}\times 2^{d}$, and normal bases of the finite field $\mathbb{F}_{2^{2^{d}}}$.

papers.title: Alleviating the Hubble tension with self-interacting ultralight dark matter
papers.abstract: We study the possibility that a self-interacting ultralight dark matter field with a characteristic energy scale $\tilde{m}\simeq 1~{\rm eV}$ can behave like an extra radiation component before recombination. This additional radiation can reduce the sound horizon of the photon-baryon fluid. A smaller sound horizon can give a higher inferred value of the present-day Hubble parameter at the background level, and thus may help reduce the Hubble tension. This effect can be obtained without adding another dark sector component besides self-interacting ULDM. A full perturbation and likelihood analysis is needed to see if the model is consistent with CMB and structure-formation data.

papers.title: Recovery guarantees for compressed sensing photoacoustic tomography
papers.abstract: Photoacoustic tomography is an emerging medical imaging technology whose primary aim is to map the high-contrast optical properties of biological tissues by leveraging high-resolution ultrasound measurements. Mathematically, this can be framed as an inverse source problem for the wave equation over a specific domain. In this work, for the first time, it is shown how, by assuming signal sparsity, it is possible to establish rigorous stable recovery guarantees when the data collection is given by spatial averages restricted to a sparse, randomly sampled portion of the boundary. Our framework encompasses many approaches that have been considered in the literature. The result is a consequence of a general framework for subsampled inverse problems developed in previous works and refined stability estimates for an inverse problem for the wave equation with surface measurements.

papers.title: Zero-shot Video Moment Retrieval via Off-the-shelf Multimodal Large Language Models
papers.abstract: The target of video moment retrieval (VMR) is predicting temporal spans within a video that semantically match a given linguistic query. Existing VMR methods based on multimodal large language models (MLLMs) overly rely on expensive high-quality datasets and time-consuming fine-tuning. Although some recent studies introduce a zero-shot setting to avoid fine-tuning, they overlook inherent language bias in the query, leading to erroneous localization. To tackle the aforementioned challenges, this paper proposes Moment-GPT, a tuning-free pipeline for zero-shot VMR utilizing frozen MLLMs. Specifically, we first employ LLaMA-3 to correct and rephrase the query to mitigate language bias. Subsequently, we design a span generator combined with MiniGPT-v2 to produce candidate spans adaptively. Finally, to leverage the video comprehension capabilities of MLLMs, we apply VideoChatGPT and span scorer to select the most appropriate spans. Our proposed method substantially outperforms the state-ofthe-art MLLM-based and zero-shot models on several public datasets, including QVHighlights, ActivityNet-Captions, and Charades-STA.

papers.title: Reduction by stages for affine W-algebras
papers.abstract: Given a pair of nilpotent orbits in a simple Lie algebra, one can associate a pair of vertex algebras called affine W-algebras. Under some compatibility conditions on these orbits, we prove that one of these W-algebras can be obtained as the quantum Hamiltonian reduction of the other. This property is called reduction by stages. We provide several examples in classical and exceptional types. To prove reduction by stages for affine W-algebras, we use our previous work on reduction by stages for the Slodowy slices associated with these nilpotent orbits, these slices being the associated varieties of the W-algebras. We also prove and use the fact that each W-algebra can be defined using several equivalent BRST cohomology constructions: choosing the right BRST complexes allows us to connect the two W-algebras in a natural way.

papers.title: CHAIR -- Classifier of Hallucination as Improver
papers.abstract: In this work, we introduce CHAIR (Classifier of Hallucination As ImproveR), a supervised framework for detecting hallucinations by analyzing internal logits from each layer of every token. Our method extracts a compact set of features such as maximum, minimum, mean, standard deviation, and slope-from the token logits across all layers, enabling effective hallucination detection without overfitting. Experiments on TruthfulQA and MMLU datasets demonstrate that CHAIR significantly improves detection accuracy, particularly in zero-shot scenarios, showcasing its robustness and generalizability. Beyond hallucination detection, CHAIR highlights the potential of using internal representations for designing advanced decoding strategies. By leveraging patterns in logits, we suggest that more sophisticated models and adaptive decoding methods could further reduce hallucinations and enhance text completion quality. CHAIR not only offers a practical solution for detecting hallucinations but also lays the groundwork for exploring richer representations in LLMs to improve their factuality and coherence.

papers.title: New Nonbinary Quantum Codes from Quasi-Twisted Codes with Scalar and Matrix Twists
papers.abstract: We construct quantum codes over nonbinary finite fields from one-generator index-$2$ quasi-twisted codes and from codes invariant under a $2\times2$ matrix twist, via the symplectic construction. For one-generator quasi-twisted codes, we give direct proofs of the dimension formulas and of matrix and polynomial tests for symplectic self-orthogonality. When the same scalar twist $λ$ acts on both blocks, we show that $λ^2\ne1$ gives only quantum distance $1$. Thus, in this construction, distance greater than $1$ requires $λ=\pm1$, corresponding to quasi-cyclic and quasi-negacyclic codes. We also study determinant-one $2\times2$ matrix twists. For twists given by companion matrices, we describe the resulting codes and their symplectic duals by polynomials over the base field. When the associated quadratic is irreducible over $\mathbb F_q$, these codes correspond to Hermitian constacyclic codes over the quadratic extension. With a rank criterion for the minimum distance and standard propagation rules, our explicit constructions present quantum codes that improve the recorded minimum-distance lower bounds for $164$ distinct entries in Grassl's tables of quantum codes over nonbinary finite fields.

papers.title: Asymptotic expansions for normal deviations of random walks conditioned to stay positive
papers.abstract: We consider a one-dimensional random walk $S_n$ having i.i.d. increments with zero mean and finite variance. We continue our study of asymptotic expansions for local probabilities $\mathbf P(S_n=x,τ_0>n)$, which has been started in \cite{DTW23}. Obtained there expansions make sense in the zone $x=o(\frac{\sqrt{n}}{\log^{1/2} n})$ only. In the present paper we derive an alternative expansion, which deals with $x$ of order $\sqrt{n}$.

papers.title: The Kähler-Ricci soliton on bounded pseudoconvex domains
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish rigidity results for Kähler--Ricci solitons on bounded pseudoconvex domains in $\mathbb C^n$. We first show that if a complete Kähler metric has $C^1$ quasi-bounded geometry and negatively pinched Ricci curvature outside a compact set, then any soliton vector field whose metric dual is closed must vanish. In particular, such a soliton is Kähler--Einstein. We then prove that any Bergman Kähler--Ricci soliton of bounded domains is Kähler--Einstein. Combined with Huang--Xiao's resolution of Cheng's conjecture, this yields a soliton analogue of Cheng's conjecture. We also provide several model domains as examples.

papers.title: A context-adaptive policy framework for robust and reactive robotic manipulation via uncertainty-aware imitation learning
papers.abstract: Generating robust and reactive manipulation strategies that can adapt to changing context information is a challenging task in robotics. Over the years, Learning from Demonstration (LfD) has emerged as an intuitive and effective solution for generating reactive policies, particularly by following dynamical-system(DS)-based approaches. However, most state-of-the-art DS-based approaches focus on addressing the robustness limitations, overlooking the modulation of policies in response to the environment. As a result, they tend to be inflexible with respect to parameterization by task-dependent variables. In this work, we build on existing work on policy fusion and uncertainty quantification to propose a context-adaptive policy framework that combines task-parameterized, robust and reactive manipulation. For this, we use LfD to acquire a policy that is conditioned on the robot state and low-dimensional task-dependent parameters reflecting the environment. We combine the learned policy with additional uncertainty-aware policies using a Mixture of Experts (MoE) formulation to improve its out-of-distribution (OOD) robustness and convergence behavior. The approach is evaluated on the LASA handwriting dataset and on a real 7-DoF robot in three scenarios: force-conditioned grasping, manipulation of deformable food items and object-centric grasping.

papers.title: Revisiting Unicity Distance: A Channel Transmission Perspective and Its Limits
papers.abstract: This paper revisits the classical notion of unicity distance for substitution ciphers from an information-theoretic perspective. We frame simple-substitution encryption as a noisy transmission channel, in which the plaintext is the message, the unknown key is the noise, and the attacker is the receiver. Using typical sets to motivate the notion of meaningful plaintexts, we apply the channel coding theorem to blocks encrypted with independent fresh keys. We show that a block length exceeding $H(K)/D$ permits reliable communication at the language's entropy rate using suitably chosen codebooks across many blocks. This provides a channel transmission interpretation of the classical unicity-distance formula. We then test how well this formula describes plaintext recovery when the message is a passage from six known novels. More than $99\%$ of the passages are uniquely identifiable at 18 letters, well before the classical estimate of about 28. N-gram language models, based on the frequencies of short letter sequences, predict the recovery probabilities much more closely. In this experiment, the classical formula misses the recovery transition, while a more detailed model of the language captures it.

papers.title: Testable leptogenesis and $0νββ$ decay in extended seesaw model
papers.abstract: We investigate the possibility of observable neutrinoless double beta decay $( 0 νββ)$ and viable leptogenesis within a low-scale extended inverse seesaw mechanism with additional sterile neutrinos. General effective field theory (EFT) considerations suggest that if there are experimentally observable signatures in $0 νββ$-decay and a lepton asymmetry generated by heavy right-handed neutrino decays, thermal leptogenesis is likely to be unviable. However, in this work, we show that in the context of low-scale leptogenesis, one can obtain the observed baryon asymmetry of the universe and observable signatures of $0 νββ$ decay in the presence of additional sterile neutrinos. In this framework, the light neutrino masses are suppressed by the extended seesaw parameter, $μ$, thereby allowing for $\mathcal{O}(10\, \mathrm{TeV})$ right-handed (RH) neutrinos, while avoiding small Yukawa couplings as in other neutrino mass models and near degeneracies in the RH neutrino spectrum as required by the low-scale leptogenesis paradigm. Contributions to the $0 νββ$-decay rate from additional sterile neutrinos can be appreciable, while the corresponding contributions to the early universe lepton asymmetry washout rate are suppressed by other parameters not entering the $0 νββ$-decay amplitudes. We show that for keV-MeV scale, sterile neutrinos future ton-scale $0νββ$-decay experiments offer potential signals while maintaining viable leptogenesis.

papers.title: Functional Flexibility in Generative AI Interfaces: Text Editing with LLMs through Conversations, Toolbars, and Prompts
papers.abstract: Many recent user interfaces (UIs) promise great flexibility via access to Large Language Models (LLMs) through prompting. This shifts efforts in accessing functionality from developers to users. However, is a maximum of functional flexibility always beneficial? We find: no -- and develop Functional Flexibility as a concept by reflecting on our long-term exploration of integrating LLMs into a text editor: In a prompt-elicitation survey, people (N=121) envisioned elaborate prompts for delegating flexible tasks to AI. In contrast, when interacting with a prototype (N=10), users preferred short command-like prompts, as prompting repeated functionality is tedious. Another prototype offered such commands in a toolbar, in addition to flexible prompting, leading users (N=12) to dynamically work with both. We contribute Functional Flexibility as a theoretical construct with analytical, critical, and constructive value. Overall, we encourage designing UIs for generative AI that go beyond free text prompting by explicitly considering functional flexibility in design.

papers.title: Faster algorithms for packing forests in graphs and related problems
papers.abstract: We consider several problems related to packing forests in graphs. The first one is to find $k$ edge-disjoint forests of maximum size in a directed graph $G$ such that the indegree of each vertex in these forests is at most $k$. We describe a min-max characterization for this problem and show that it can be solved in almost linear time for fixed $k$, extending the algorithm of [Gabow, 1995]. Specifically, the complexity is $O(k δm \log n)$, where $n, m$ are the numbers of vertices and edges in $G$, respectively, and $δ= \max\{1, k - k_G\}$, where $k_G$ is the edge connectivity of the graph. Using our solution to this problem, we obtain algorithms for two applications: (1) The $k$-forest problem: find $k$ forests in an undirected graph $G$ maximizing the number of edges in their union. We show how to solve this problem in $O(k^3 \min\{kn, m\} \log^2 n + k \cdot{\rm MAXFLOW}(m, m) \log n)$ time, breaking the $O_k(n^{3/2})$ complexity barrier of previously known approaches. (2) The Directed edge-connectivity augmentation problem: find a smallest set of directed edges whose addition to the given directed graph makes it strongly $k$-connected. We give a deterministic algorithm with complexity $O(k δm \log n)+T_{\rm split}$, where $T_{\rm split}$ is the time to split off one vertex in a graph with $O(m+δn)$ edges while preserving strong connectivity among the original vertices. For Eulerian directed graphs, the total complexity is $O(k δm \log n)$. A similar approach solves the undirected version of the problem in $O(k δm \log n)$ time.

papers.title: Backbone coloring for graphs with degree 4
papers.abstract: The $λ$-backbone coloring of a graph $G$ with backbone $H$ is a proper vertex coloring in which the endpoints of every edge from $H$ are assigned colors which differ by at least $λ$. In this paper we prove that $BBC_λ(G,H)\leλ+5$ for every graph $G$ with maximum degree at most $4$ and every connected spanning bipartite backbone $H$, provided that $λ\ge3$. A suitable coloring can be found in linear time. The bound is sharp for $λ\ge4$, even for spanning tree backbones. The proof combines degree-list coloring with a balanced choice of vertices in an auxiliary bipartite multigraph. We also settle the previously open complexity status for graphs with maximum degree $4$ and connected bipartite backbones, proving NP-completeness even for spanning tree backbones for every fixed $λ\ge2$. Furthermore, we obtain an almost complete classification of the complexity of deciding whether $BBC_λ(G,H)\le k$ for graphs with maximum degree at most $4$ and matching, galaxy, Hamiltonian path, and spanning tree backbones. We also determine the effect of allowing isolated vertices in matching and galaxy backbones.

papers.title: Nontrivial Riemann Zeros as Spectrum
papers.abstract: We present the Riemann operator $ \hat{\mathcal{R}} $, a densely defined non-symmetric operator acting on $ L^2([0,\infty)) $ whose point spectrum is given by the nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function $ ζ(s) $: \[ σ_{\mathrm{p}}(\hat{\mathcal{R}})=\left\{i\left(ρ-1/2\right)\midρ\in\mathcal{Z}_ζ\right\}, \qquad \mathcal{Z}_ζ:=\left\{ρ\midζ(ρ)=0,\;0<\Re(ρ)<1\right\} \, . \] We prove the existence of a linear operator $ \hat{W} $ that intertwines the Riemann operator $ \hat{\mathcal{R}} $ with its Hilbert-space adjoint $ \hat{\mathcal{R}}^* $, i.e., $ \hat{\mathcal{R}}\,\hat{W}=\hat{W}\,\hat{\mathcal{R}}^* $. Strict positivity of the intertwiner $ \hat{W} $ is equivalent to the Riemann Hypothesis together with the simplicity of the nontrivial zeros: \[ \hat{W}>0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\Re(ρ)=1/2\;\text{ and }\;ζ^{(1)}(ρ)\neq0\qquad\forall\,ρ\in\mathcal{Z}_ζ\, . \]

papers.title: Guard Analysis and Safe Erasure Gradual Typing: a Type System for Elixir
papers.abstract: We formalize a new type system for Elixir, a dynamically typed functional programming language of growing popularity that runs on the Erlang virtual machine. Our system combines gradual typing with semantic subtyping to enable precise, sound, and practical static type analysis, without requiring any changes to Elixir's compilation pipeline or runtime. Type soundness is ensured by leveraging runtime checks -- both implicit, from the Erlang VM, and explicit, via developer-written guards. Central to our approach are two key innovations: the notion of "strong functions", which can be assigned precise types even when applied to inputs that may fall outside their intended domain; and a fine-grained analysis of guards that enables accurate type refinement for case expressions and guarded function definitions. While type information is erased before execution and not used by the compiler, our "safe erasure" gradual typing strategy maintains soundness and expressiveness without compromising compatibility or performance. This work lays the theoretical foundation for Elixir's new type system, outlines its integration into recent versions of the language, and demonstrates its effectiveness on large-scale industrial codebases.

papers.title: A polytopal discontinuous Galerkin method for the pseudo-stress formulation of the unsteady Stokes problem
papers.abstract: This work aims to construct and analyze a discontinuous Galerkin method on polytopal grids (PolydG) to solve the pseudo-stress formulation of the unsteady Stokes problem. The pseudo-stress variable is introduced due to the growing interest in non-Newtonian flows and coupled interface problems, where stress assumes a fundamental role. The space-time discretization of the problem is achieved by combining the PolydG approach with the implicit theta-method time integration scheme. For both the semi- and fully-discrete problems we present a detailed stability analysis. Moreover, we derive convergence estimates for the fully discrete space-time discretization. A set of verification tests is presented to verify the theoretical estimates and the application of the method to cases of engineering interest.

papers.title: Monotonicity properties of Hadamard weighted geometric means of bounded sets of positive kernel operators
papers.abstract: We prove new monotonicity properties for joint and generalized spectral radius and their essential versions, operator norm, Hausdorff measure of non-compactness and numerical radius of products and sums of Hadamard weighted geometric means of positive kernel operators on appropriate Banach function spaces. Our results extend recent results on weighted geometric symmetrizations of bounded sets of such operators defined on $L^2$. To our knowledge, several proved properties in this generality are new even in the finite dimensional case and also in the case of singelton sets.

papers.title: H(curl)-based approximation of the Stokes problem with slip boundary conditions
papers.abstract: Reformulating the incompressible Stokes equations with the velocity sought in H(curl) has recently emerged as a promising approach for the design of helicity-preserving schemes in magnetohydrodynamics and pressure-robust finite element methods on polygonal meshes. A key challenge in this setting, however, is the treatment of Navier slip boundary conditions. In this paper, we overcome this difficulty by recasting the slip condition as a Robin boundary condition and proving well-posedness (up to a finite-dimensional kernel) of the resulting continuous problem. We further identify the geometric and regularity assumptions on the domain and the exact solution under which the classical Stokes solution is recovered. Finally, we study a finite element Galerkin discretization, establishing stability and a priori error estimates. Numerical experiments validate the optimal convergence rates predicted by the theory.

papers.title: The Baire property and precompact duality
papers.abstract: We prove that if $G$ is a totally bounded abelian group \st\ its dual group $\widehat{G}_p$ equipped with the finite-open topology is a Baire group, then every compact subset of $G$ must be finite. This solves an open question by Chasco, Domínguez and Tkachenko. {Among other consequences, we obtain an example of a group that is $g$-dense in its completion but is not $g$-barrelled. This solves a question proposed by Au$β$enhofer and Dikranjan.}

papers.title: Super Guarding and Dark Rays in Art Galleries
papers.abstract: We explore an Art Gallery variant where each point of a polygon must be seen by k guards, and guards cannot see through other guards. Surprisingly, even covering convex polygons under this variant is not straightforward. For example, covering every point in a triangle k=4 times (a 4-cover) requires 5 guards, and achieving a 10-cover requires 12 guards. Our main result is tight bounds on k-covering a convex polygon of n vertices, for all k and n. The proofs of both upper and lower bounds are nontrivial. We also obtain bounds for simple polygons, leaving tight bounds an open problem.

papers.title: Uncovering the mechanism of chiral three-nucleon force in driving spin-orbit splitting
papers.abstract: The three-nucleon force (3NF) is crucial in shaping the shell structure of atomic nuclei, particularly impacting the enhancement of spin-orbit (SO) splitting, especially in nuclei with significant deviations from stability. Despite its importance, the specific mechanisms driving this enhancement remain unclear. In this study, we introduce a decomposition scheme based on the rank of irreducible tensors forming the 3NF, derived from chiral effective field theory at next-to-next-to-leading order, to elucidate their influence on SO splitting. Within the shell-model framework, our analysis reveals that the rank-1 component of the 3NF is the primary factor enlarging the energy gap between the $0p_{3/2}$ and $0p_{1/2}$ single-particle levels in $p$-shell nuclei. Since the rank-1 component originates exclusively from the $2π$-exchange 3NF, our finding will not depend on the choice of the low-energy constants of contact terms. We also remark on the antisymmetry of the rank-1 3NF, which can affect the quantum entanglement of spin states. This study lays the groundwork for further exploration into this field toward a microscopic understanding of the 3NF impact on the nuclear shell structure.

papers.title: On the Unipotent $p$-adic Simpson Correspondence
papers.abstract: The goal of this paper is to show a (derived) $p$-adic Simpson correspondence for (locally) unipotent coefficients on smooth rigid-analytic varieties. Our results depend on a deformation to $\mathbf{B}_\mathtt{dr}^+/ξ^2$, and not on a choice of exponential (as required for more general coefficients). Our methods are higher categorical, hinging on the theory of modules over $\mathbf{E}_\infty$-algebras.

papers.title: Critical-Point Characterization of Rank-Constrained Optimization and Global Convergence of Projected Gradient Descent
papers.abstract: We study the rank-constrained problem $\min_{\mathrm{rank}(\mathbf{X})\leq r} f(\mathbf{X})$ when the unconstrained minimizer $\mathbf{X}_*$ has rank $r_*\leq r$. We apply a sharp matrix inequality to characterize critical points and establish deterministic global linear convergence of projected gradient descent (ProjGD). First, assuming that $f$ satisfies rank-$(r+r_*)$ restricted smoothness and strong convexity with constants $L$ and $μ$, respectively, where $0<μ<L$, we show that every nonoptimal rank-$r$ critical point satisfies the inequality $\|P_{T(\mathbf{X})^\perp}\nabla f(\mathbf{X})\|/σ_r(\mathbf{X}) \geq (2Lμ/(L-μ))\sqrt{r/r_*}$. Here $P_{T(\mathbf{X})^\perp}\nabla f(\mathbf{X})$ is the component of the gradient normal to the tangent space $T(\mathbf{X})$ and $σ_r(\mathbf{X})$ is the $r$-th singular value of $\mathbf{X}$. Second, this inequality implies that $\mathbf{X}_*$ is the unique fixed point of ProjGD whenever the step size $η$ satisfies $η>\sqrt{r_*/r}(L-μ)/(2Lμ)$. Finally, under an additional rank-$2r$ restricted smoothness assumption, we apply the argument to the actual ProjGD iterates, establish a uniform improvement estimate for every iteration, and prove deterministic global linear convergence from every initialization of rank at most $r$ for $\sqrt{r_*/r}(L-μ)/(2Lμ)<η<1/L$. The result allows arbitrary rank overparameterization $r\geq r_*$, and its convergence rate is independent of the singular-value condition number of $\mathbf{X}_*$. As a consequence, a rank-preserving curve argument proves the no-spurious-local-minima property whenever $(L-μ)/(L+μ)<(1+\sqrt{r_*/r})^{-1}$. This matches the sharp threshold established by McRae et al. (2026). A quadratic example shows that the lower bound on the step size $\sqrt{r_*/r}(L-μ)/(2Lμ)$ is also sharp.

papers.title: QANAD: A Model-Driven Framework for Quantitative Analysis and Synthesis of Activity Diagrams via Probabilistic Model Checking
papers.abstract: Probabilistic model checking is a widely used formal verification technique to automatically verify qualitative and quantitative QoS properties for probabilistic models, such as reliability, performance, and cost. However, devising suitable and representative models for systems of interest in model checkers, writing corresponding properties, and verifying them requires domain knowledge in probabilistic models, formal verification, and the target model checkers. This unavoidably makes model checking not easily accessible for researchers and engineers who may lack the required knowledge. Previous work has extended UML activity diagrams with probability and time, along with quality annotations, developed transformations from activity diagrams to probabilistic models which model checkers support, and implemented accompanying tools for automation. The research, however, is fragmented, informal, or not fully open, making its use, extension, and adaptation non-trivial. To mitigate these challenges, we introduce QANAD, a comprehensive verification framework for activity diagrams, that includes a new profile for probability, time, parameters, and quality annotations, a semantics interpretation of activity diagrams in Markov models variants (DTMCs, MDPs, and CTMCs) and their parametric versions, and a set of formal transformation rules from activity diagrams to the PRISM modelling language, supported by the leading model checkers PRISM and Storm. The theory underpinning QANAD has been realised into transformation implementation using model-driven engineering, enabling fully automated model transformation with automated verification using (parametric) probabilistic model checking and semi-automated synthesis. We demonstrate QANAD on a case study where multiple robots are used for delivery in a hospital environment and evaluated six other examples from the literature.

papers.title: Pseudo-random Instance Generators in C++ for Deterministic and Stochastic Multi-commodity Network Design Problems
papers.abstract: Network design problems constitute an important family of combinatorial optimization problems for which many exact and heuristic algorithms have been developed over the last few decades. Two central problems in this family are the multi-commodity, capacitated, fixed charge network design problem (MCFNDP) and its stochastic counterpart, the two-stage stochastic MCFNDP with recourse. These are standard problems that often serve as workbenches for devising and testing models and algorithms in stylized but near-realistic settings. Progress on solution methods requires instances of varying size, structure and difficulty. We present two open-source C++ generators. The deterministic generator modernizes and extends the generator underlying the Canad instances, with new topologies and continuous control of capacity tightness and cost structure. The stochastic generator, which is to our knowledge the first publicly available one for the two-stage stochastic MCFNDP, builds scenarios that match user-specified moments and correlations. We also release libraries of configurations for 6,000 deterministic and 416 stochastic instances, as well as the base instances and configurations of 20 stochastic instances on hub-and-spoke benchmark networks. The generators aim to support systematic and reproducible experimentation, including the training and out-of-sample evaluation of learning-based and stochastic programming methods.

papers.title: Associativity conditions for linear quasigroups and equivalence relations on binary trees
papers.abstract: We characterise the bracketing identities satisfied by linear quasigroups with the help of certain equivalence relations on binary trees that are based on the left and right depths of the leaves modulo some integers. The numbers of equivalence classes of $n$-leaf binary trees are variants of the Catalan numbers, and they form the associative spectrum (a kind of measure of non-associativity) of a quasigroup. Every group-based equivalence relation arising here can be replaced by one defined by an abelian group generated by at most two elements. The fine associative spectra form a lattice isomorphic to the lattice of rank-two subgroups of $\mathbb{Z}^2$ with an additional least element. This classifies the equivalence relations completely; closed formulas for all their numbers of classes remain open.

papers.title: OpinionGPT: Modelling Explicit Biases in Instruction-Tuned LLMs
papers.abstract: Instruction-tuned Large Language Models (LLMs) have recently showcased remarkable ability to generate fitting responses to natural language instructions. However, an open research question concerns the inherent biases of trained models and their responses. For instance, if the data used to tune an LLM is dominantly written by persons with a specific political bias, we might expect generated answers to share this bias. Current research work seeks to de-bias such models, or suppress potentially biased answers. With this demonstration, we take a different view on biases in instruction-tuning: Rather than aiming to suppress them, we aim to make them explicit and transparent. To this end, we present OpinionGPT, a web demo in which users can ask questions and select all biases they wish to investigate. The demo will answer this question using a model fine-tuned on text representing each of the selected biases, allowing side-by-side comparison. To train the underlying model, we identified 11 different biases (political, geographic, gender, age) and derived an instruction-tuning corpus in which each answer was written by members of one of these demographics. This paper presents OpinionGPT, illustrates how we trained the bias-aware model and showcases the web application (available at https://opiniongpt.informatik.hu-berlin.de).

papers.title: Euler characteristics and moderateness of Fujiki--Oka resolutions
papers.abstract: Fujiki--Oka resolutions of cyclic quotient singularities of type $\frac{1}{r}(1,a_2,\ldots,a_n)$ are constructed using multidimensional continued fractions. In this paper, we compute the Euler characteristics of Fujiki--Oka resolutions in arbitrary dimension using the heights of the coefficients of the associated remainder polynomials. We also give a necessary and sufficient condition for moderateness of Fujiki--Oka resolutions in dimension three.

papers.title: Normative Ceilings and Stochastic Giving
papers.abstract: People randomize when they allocate money to others, and what else is available changes how they randomize: adding an alternative can raise the probability that an existing one is chosen, in violation of Regularity. We characterize a model of stochastic choice in which a selfish decision maker faces norm-driven social pressure and the menu matters only through one scalar, the normative ceiling, defined as the most pro-social alternative available. We introduce two conditions on cross-menu comparisons: comparisons line up through a single rescaling attached to each menu's most normative alternative, and higher normative levels are more selective. Together with standard positivity, continuity, acyclicity, order and richness requirements, these conditions force the randomization cost to depend on the menu only through the ceiling. Raising the ceiling makes the cost uniformly more curved. Random utility and baseline perturbed utility models imply Regularity; models of deliberate randomization necessarily violate it; ours does neither. Instead, our model predicts that Regularity can fail only when the ceiling rises across behaviorally distinguishable levels, and that it then fails at the least selfish alternatives. This prediction is a sign restriction with no free parameters, and we show how nested menus test it.

papers.title: Monodromy groups of Jacobians with definite quaternionic multiplication
papers.abstract: Let $A$ be an abelian variety over a number field. The connected monodromy field of $A$ is the minimal field over which the images of all the $\ell$-adic torsion representations have connected Zariski closure. We show that for all even $g \geq 4$, there exist infinitely many geometrically nonisogenous abelian varieties $A$ over $\mathbb{Q}$ of dimension $g$ where the connected monodromy field is strictly larger than the field of definition of the endomorphisms of $A$. Our construction arises from explicit families of hyperelliptic Jacobians with definite quaternionic multiplication.

papers.title: Structure theorem for cofibrant tame functors indexed by posets of dimension 1
papers.abstract: In this paper, we discuss certain circumstances in which the category of tame functors inherits an abelian category structure with minimal resolutions and a model category structure with minimal cofibrant replacements. We also present a structure theorem for cofibrant objects in the category of tame functors indexed by realizations of posets of dimension 1 with values in the category of chain complexes in an abelian category whose all objects are projectives. Moreover, we introduce a general technique to generate indecomposable objects in the abelian category of functors indexed by finite posets.

papers.title: A Simple Proof of the Riemann Hypothesis
papers.abstract: In this article, it is proved that the non-trivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function must lie on the critical line, known as the Riemann hypothesis.

papers.title: Where the Model Frequently Meets the Road: Combining Statistical, Formal, and Case Study Methods
papers.abstract: This paper briefly analyzes the working or default assumptions researchers in the formal, statistical, and case study traditions typically hold regarding the sources of unexplained variance, parameter values, functional forms, time, and external validity. We argue that these working assumptions are often not essential to each method, and that these assumptions can be relaxed in ways that allow multimethod work to proceed. We then analyze the comparative advantages of different combinations of formal, statistical, and case study methods, and offer advice on how to combine these methods.

papers.title: Quadratic Gradient: Accelerating Privacy-Preserving Logistic Regression Training with Homomorphic Encryption
papers.abstract: Training logistic regression over encrypted data has emerged as a prominent approach to addressing security concerns in recent years. In this paper, we introduce an efficient gradient variant, termed the \textit{quadratic gradient}, which is specifically designed for privacy-preserving logistic regression while remaining equally effective in plaintext optimization. By incorporating this quadratic gradient, we enhance Nesterov's Accelerated Gradient (NAG), Adaptive Gradient (AdaGrad), and Adam algorithms. We evaluate these enhanced algorithms across various datasets, with experimental results demonstrating state-of-the-art convergence rates that significantly outperform traditional first-order gradient methods. Furthermore, we apply the enhanced NAG method to implement homomorphic logistic regression training, achieving comparable performance within only four iterations. The proposed quadratic-gradient approach offers a unified framework that synergizes the advantages of first-order gradient methods and second-order Newton-type methods, suggesting broad applicability to diverse numerical optimization tasks.

papers.title: On the Global Convergence of Gradient Descent for multi-layer ResNets in the mean-field regime
papers.abstract: Finding the optimal configuration of parameters in ResNet is a nonconvex minimization problem, but first-order methods often find the global optimum when the network is overparameterized and the training algorithm is run for sufficiently many iterations. We study this phenomenon in the mean-field regime, where the network can be described approximately by an ordinary integral equation (OIE) and the training process of ResNet becomes a gradient-flow partial differential equation (PDE). Under the condition that the activation function is $2$-homogeneous or partially $1$-homogeneous, we show that this gradient-flow PDE converges to the global minimum. This result suggests that if the ResNet is sufficiently large, first-order optimization methods can find global minimizers that fit the training data as well. Further, by controlling the generalization error, we prove that the gradient-flow PDE is stable with respect to its cost function, implying that a finite-sized but sufficiently large dataset drawn from the underlying data distribution can exhibit the properties of the continuous limit. We give lower bounds on the depth and width of the network for the gradient-flow approximation to hold. We also lower-bound the size of the training data set needed to attain accurate approximation.

papers.title: Harmonic mean closed vector lattices
papers.abstract: We introduce the notion of the harmonic mean on certain Archimedean vector lattices, which we call harmonic mean closed. Using this concept, we provide a new characterization of positive orthogonally additive polynomials from a harmonic mean closed Archimedean vector lattice to a uniformly complete Archimedean vector lattice space entirely in terms of harmonic means. This result yields polynomial versions of the QM-AM-GM-HM inequalities on Archimedean vector lattices where the only additional requirement on the domain space is that it is harmonic mean closed.

papers.title: A Certified Reduced Basis Method for Linear Parametrized Parabolic Optimal Control Problems in Space-Time Formulation
papers.abstract: In this work, we propose to efficiently solve time dependent parametrized optimal control problems governed by parabolic partial differential equations through the certified reduced basis method. In particular, we will exploit an error estimator procedure, based on easy-to-compute quantities which guarantees a rigorous and efficient bound for the error of the involved variables. First, we propose analyzing the problem at hand, proving its well-posedness thanks to Ne\v cas - Babu\v ska theory in a space-time formulation. Then, we derive error estimators to apply a Greedy method during the offline stage, to perform, during the online stage, a Galerkin projection onto a low-dimensional space spanned by properly chosen high-fidelity solutions. We tested the error estimators on two model problems governed by a Graetz flow with physical and geometrical parametrization. The results have been compared to a previously proposed bound, based on the exact computation of the Babu\v ska inf-sup constant, in terms of reliability and computational costs. We remark that our findings still hold in the steady setting, and we also propose a brief insight for this simpler formulation.

papers.title: Sharp relations between volume growth, isoperimetry and escape probability in vertex-transitive graphs
papers.abstract: We prove sharp bounds on the probability that the simple random walk on a vertex-transitive graph escapes the ball of radius $r$ before returning to its starting point. In particular, this shows that if the ball of radius $r$ has size slightly greater than quadratic in $r$ then this probability is bounded from below. On the other hand, we show that if the ball of radius $r$ has volume slightly less than cubic in $r$ then this probability decays logarithmically for all larger balls. These results represent a finitary refinement of Varopoulos's theorem that a random walk on a vertex-transitive graph is recurrent if and only if the graph has at most quadratic volume growth. They also imply the existence of a gap at $0$ for escape probabilities: there exists a universal constant $c>0$ such that the random walk on an arbitrary vertex-transitive graph is either recurrent or has a probability of at least $c$ of escaping to infinity. We also prove versions of these results for finite graphs, in particular confirming and strengthening a conjecture of Benjamini and Kozma from 2002. Amongst other things, we also generalise our results to give a sharp finitary version of the characterisation of $p$-parabolic vertex-transitive graphs, prove a number of sharp isoperimetric inequalities for vertex-transitive graphs, and prove a locality result for the escape probability of the random walk on a vertex-transitive graph that can be seen as an analogue of Schramm's locality conjecture for the critical percolation probability.

papers.title: Revisiting the Graph Isomorphism Problem with Semidefinite Programming
papers.abstract: It is well-known that two graphs $G_1$ and $G_2$ on $n$ vertices are isomorphic if and only if their compatibility graph, an auxiliary graph on $n^2$ vertices, contains a clique of order $n$. In this paper, we give an exact conic formulation of this clique problem. We show that $G_1$ and $G_2$ are isomorphic if and only if a system of linear constraints over the cone of completely positive matrices is feasible. Since deciding membership in the completely positive cone is NP-hard, this formulation does not by itself yield an efficient algorithm. Relaxing complete positivity to positive semidefiniteness yields a semidefinite program whose infeasibility certifies that the two graphs are not isomorphic. We establish basic properties of this relaxation. Specifically, it is at least as strong as the necessary condition given by the Lovász $\vartheta$ number of the complement of the compatibility graph, it never admits a strictly feasible solution, and it is implied by the degree-two level of the Lasserre hierarchy applied to a natural integer formulation of graph isomorphism. In light of known lower bounds for the Lasserre hierarchy, the latter indicates that the relaxation cannot decide isomorphism for all pairs of graphs. We leave open the question of characterizing the pairs of graphs for which the relaxation is tight.

papers.title: On the interplay between noise and curvature and its effect on optimization and generalization
papers.abstract: The speed at which one can minimize an expected loss using stochastic methods depends on two properties: the curvature of the loss and the variance of the gradients. While most previous works focus on one or the other of these properties, we explore how their interaction affects optimization speed. Further, as the ultimate goal is good generalization performance, we clarify how both curvature and noise are relevant to properly estimate the generalization gap. Realizing that the limitations of some existing works stems from a confusion between these matrices, we also clarify the distinction between the Fisher matrix, the Hessian, and the covariance matrix of the gradients.

papers.title: $L^p-L^q$ estimates for maximal operators associated to families of finite type curves
papers.abstract: We investigate the \(L^p\)-\(L^q\) boundedness of maximal operators associated with averages over families of finite-type curves in the plane. These operators are defined by \[ \mathbb{M}f(x):=\sup_{1\leq t\leq 2} \left|\int_{\mathbb{C}}f(x-ty)ρ(y)\,dσ(y)\right|, \] where \(dσ\) denotes the normalized Lebesgue measure on the curve \(\mathbb{C}\), and \(ρ\) is a smooth cutoff function. Let \(\triangle\) denote the closed triangle with vertices \[ P=\left(\frac25,\frac15\right),\qquad Q=\left(\frac12,\frac12\right),\qquad R=(0,0). \] We establish that, whenever \[ \left(\frac1p,\frac1q\right) \in \bigl(\triangle\setminus\{P,Q\}\bigr) \cap \left\{ \left(\frac1p,\frac1q\right): \frac1p<\frac2q,\quad p>\frac{(m+1)q}{q+1} \right\}, \] there exists a constant \(B>0\) such that \[ \|\mathbb{M}f\|_{L^q(\mathbb{R}^2)} \leq B\|f\|_{L^p(\mathbb{R}^2)}. \] As an application, we derive \(L^p\)-\(L^q\) estimates for solutions of higher-order strictly hyperbolic pseudodifferential equations.

papers.title: Circuit spectra for binary matroids
papers.abstract: The circuit spectrum of a matroid is defined to be the set of circuit sizes. The circuit $e$-spectrum of a matroid is the set of circuit sizes of the matroid containing the element $e$. The circuit spectrum problem is an important problem. Erdős (1992) conjectured that every connected graph $G$ with girth $g$ and average degree $d$ has a cycle spectrum of size at least $Ω(d^{\lfloor (g-1)/2 \rfloor})$. Sudakov and Verstraëte (2008) proved the full conjecture of Erdős in a stronger form. It is natural to consider the size of the circuit spectra of binary matroids. Murty (1971) characterized all connected binary matroids with circuit spectra of size one. Lemos et al. (2011) characterized the connected binary matroids with circuit spectra of size two, where the largest size is odd. For general binary matroids, it is still an open question to find a lower bound for the size of the circuit spectra. In this paper, we give best-possible such lower bounds for connected binary matroids that do not contain both the Fano matroid and its dual as minors. Let $M$ be a simple connected binary matroid that does not have both the Fano matroid and its dual as a minor, and $d\geq 3$ be the minimum cocircuit size of $M$. We prove that (1) for each element $e$ of $M$, the circuit $e$-spectrum of $M$ must have size at least $d-2$. This bound is best possible. (2) The circuit spectrum of $M$ must have size at least $d-1$, unless $M\cong F_7,F_7^*,R_{10}$. In exceptional cases, the spectrum of $M$ has size equal to $d-2$.

papers.title: Grana: Compositional Reward Modeling for Long-Horizon Robot Manipulation
papers.abstract: Robot reward modeling faces two challenges: generalizing across tasks and accurately tracking progress in long-horizon manipulation. General-purpose reward models demonstrate broad task transfer, but transfer from short-task pretraining to long-horizon tasks remains underexplored. Long-horizon progress models often rely on task-specific subtask classifiers or fixed action vocabularies, limiting the reuse of learned progress knowledge when adapting to new tasks. To address these challenges, we introduce Grana, a vision-language robot reward model that learns to identify unfinished subtasks and estimate their continuous progress using open-vocabulary subtask descriptions. We train a language-conditioned model to estimate progress in short-horizon tasks and individual subtasks of long-horizon tasks. For long-horizon tasks, we combine the selected subtask's predicted progress with credit for preceding completed subtasks to estimate whole-task progress. General progress prediction requires training the model across diverse tasks with progress supervision that accounts for imperfect execution. Elapsed-time proxies can misrepresent progress when relative subtask durations vary, or failures reverse local progress. We therefore introduce an annotation protocol that converts sparse subtask boundaries and action-quality annotations into dense progress targets, without requiring annotators to assign numerical progress scores. Pretraining with this supervision on 200 diverse, mostly short-horizon manipulation tasks enables zero-shot reward prediction on unseen tasks and improves progress prediction after adaptation to multi-minute, long-horizon tasks. Experiments demonstrate (i) generalizable reward prediction, including adaptation to five long-horizon tasks, (ii) benefits from pretraining and composing subtask progress estimates, and (iii) improved downstream policy performance.

papers.title: Asymptotic probabilities in random Latin squares
papers.abstract: We introduce some new general techniques for studying asymptotic probabilities in random Latin squares. Using these techniques, we obtain an asymptotic formula for the probability that a given 'small' partial Latin square $H$ is present in a uniformly random $n\times n$ Latin square (as conjectured by Divoux-Kelly-Kennedy-Sidhu). As applications, we determine which configurations are likely to appear in random Latin squares (resolving a conjecture of Allsop-Morris), we determine the asymptotic distribution of the number of $3\times 3$ Latin subsquares in a uniformly random $n\times n$ Latin square (resolving conjectures of McKay-Wanless and Kwan-Sah-Sawhney), and we show that the first two rows of a random $n\times n$ Latin square are statistically indistinguishable from a random derangement (answering a conjecture of Cameron and Cavenagh-Greenhill-Wanless).

papers.title: Cyclic Self-Dual Codes over Prime-Square Rings and Unimodular Lattices
papers.abstract: We present an explicit construction of cyclic Euclidean self-dual codes over $\mathbb{Z}/p^{2}\mathbb{Z}$, where $p$ is an odd prime, and use Construction~A to obtain unimodular lattices with large minimum norms. The construction is based on reciprocal factorizations of $x^n-1$. We explicitly describe the associated residue and torsion codes and analyze the relationship between minimum Euclidean weights and lattice minimum norms. We construct a unimodular lattice of minimum norm~$4$ in dimension~$49$, unimodular lattices of minimum norm~$5$ in dimensions $53$, $55$, $58$, $59$, and~$61$, and extremal unimodular lattices of minimum norm~$6$ in dimensions $69$ and~$71$. Using shadow theory and harmonic theta series, we prove that extremal unimodular lattices do not exist in dimensions $59$ and~$61$. Together with the known upper bounds, these results establish the optimality of the constructed lattices in all eight dimensions. In particular, we determine the previously unknown optimal minimum norms of unimodular lattices in five dimensions: $53$, $55$, $61$, $69$, and~$71$. We further construct unimodular lattices whose minimum norms are exactly one below the corresponding extremal bounds in dimensions $62$, $63$, $65$, $67$, $70$, $89$, $91$, $92$, $93$, and~$94$.

papers.title: MLE Agents: Autonomous ML Engineering in Large-scale Recommendation Systems
papers.abstract: The typical workflow for improving large-scale ranking and recommendation models is slow and tedious: an engineer forms a hypothesis, implements it as a code change, trains a model, and evaluates it both offline and online, often relying on their own intuition and experience along the way. Autonomous LLM agents promise to speed this up by running the loop on their own, but it is still unclear whether they can do this in industry-scale systems rather than on benchmarks or small proxy tasks. We build human-on-the-loop machine learning engineer (MLE) agents that propose, implement, train, and evaluate model changes on large-scale search rankers. Engineers retain control over objective design, search direction, and final-model review. We identify three obstacles that make this industry setting challenging: feedback takes hours per experiment, offline metrics do not always predict online impact, and improvements saturate after the early wins. We address these with parallel training runs, an objective calibrated to match online impact, and careful context engineering. In one campaign, the system ran 1,097 completed candidate experiments and accepted 325, a 29.6\% acceptance rate compared with 15.6\% in the earlier campaign under a different objective and search constraint. Its best model increases search volume by 0.23\% in an A/B test of large scale. Several improvements were architectural changes the team had never tried, drawn from the broader industry and literature, suggesting that MLE agents can explore regions of the design space that human intuition overlooks. We find that the design of the harness around the model matters: intuition suggests that a stronger underlying model is enough, but in our experience, the design of the loop around it is just as critical. More broadly, our work shows that autonomous agents can do real machine-learning engineering in industry-scale systems.

papers.title: AI, Specialization, and the Organization of Knowledge Work: Evidence from Legal Services
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence makes specialized knowledge cheaper to use, but its effects on professional-service firms depend on how clients reallocate work and how suppliers respond. We develop a framework linking individual self-provision, enterprise make-or-buy decisions, and pricing by specialist firms. As AI improves lower-priced alternatives, clients may reallocate work across outside providers without bringing it in-house. If the departing work is more price-sensitive than the work that remains, premium firms may raise their optimal markups even as their share of work declines. We examine these margins in U.S. legal services.
